scope: 100 fresh cases: 50 seeded random and 50 diagnostic; all inputs and all proposals read. Mixed sample is not an unbiased corpus error-rate estimate. Assistant review is not independent human gold.

baseline_comparison.warning: Case-level overlap, not exact-patch accuracy. Baseline includes segmentation policy errors; some detections only partial. Additional issues found after seeing API output are excluded from this denominator.

recommendation: Useful triage detector; reject automatic repairs/publication. Clarify remaining small-clause/dative/null-target conventions and audit boundaries separately. Batch-size pilot pending.

proposal.explanation: A comma is missing after the introductory conditional clause, making the boundary between the clauses unclear.
proposal.correction: Add a comma after “this”: “If I do all this, do you think…”

findings.note: Comma suggestion is not a demonstrated parse defect; clauses already separated structurally.

baseline.structural_issue: John is a vocative, not a nominal adverbial.
sir is a vocative, not a nominal adverbial.

baseline.semantic_caution: Acknowledgment may confirm earlier talking; not a generic completed event.

baseline.structural_issue: bring the car in: in is a particle; kilometers expresses service frequency, not the object of in.

proposal.explanation: “Bring your car in” uses the separated particle construction “bring in”; “in” is incorrectly attached as a preposition, and the construction is marked unseparated.
proposal.correction: Attach “in” as the particle of “bring” (dep=prt) and mark the construction as separated=true.

findings.note: Fix in to prt AND detach kilometers from in to a frequency adjunct of bring; proposal alone leaves an invalid particle object.

baseline.semantic_caution: Propositional agreement.

baseline.structural_issue: had better: contracted d is have, not would. Departure is intended, not established.

proposal.explanation: In “I’d better,” ’d means “had,” not “would”; the supplied lemma and modal tag misanalyze the contraction.
proposal.correction: Analyze ’d as had and revise its tag accordingly.

findings.note: Use lemma have for contracted had in had better, not literal lemma had; preserve surface.

baseline.source_issue: crescive is a rare real word but inappropriate/uncertain here; do not invent replacement.

proposal.explanation: “Crescive” is an unusual adjective meaning increasing and seems ill-suited here, but the intended wording cannot be established from context.
proposal.correction: Check whether “crescive” was intended; no specific replacement is supported.

findings.note: Rare word is contextually questionable; no justified replacement.

baseline.semantic_caution: Elliptical question about tipping cab drivers/porters.

baseline.structural_issue: Wish me luck is ditransitive: me is recipient and luck direct object; the proposed small clause is unsupported.

proposal.explanation: In “Wish me luck,” “me” and “luck” are objects of “wish,” not a subject and complement forming a clause.
proposal.correction: Attach “me” as an object of “Wish” and “luck” as its direct object.

findings.note: Recipient me and object luck attach to wish; this is not the permitted resultative small-clause case.

baseline.structural_issue: like in What is it like is not a lexical verb meaning enjoy.

proposal.explanation: In “What’s it like,” “like” is an adjective serving as the predicate complement, not a verb.
proposal.correction: Change “like” to ADJ; retain its complement attachment.

findings.note: Non-verbal like is required; the remaining subject and infinitive attachments also need adjudication. Do not use this as a ready patch.

baseline.structural_issue: Sir is a vocative, not an adverbial of the currency amount.
baseline.source_issue: RIB likely currency OCR error for RMB; source review separate from syntax.

proposal.explanation: “Sir” is a vocative, not a modifier of “RIB.”
proposal.correction: Attach “Sir” as a vocative to the clause.

findings.note: Vocative Sir; separate source currency ambiguity remains.

baseline.source_issue: The Johnson are likely requires Johnsons; retain source until verified.

proposal.explanation: The reply identifies them as a couple, so the surname appears to refer to the family; the standard plural form is missing its final “s.”
proposal.correction: Change “Johnson” to “Johnsons” if the family is intended.

findings.note: Context says couple; likely missing surname plural. Source correction needs separate rebasing.

baseline.structural_issue: Existential paid holidays misparsed as a passive event with paid as root.

proposal.explanation: “Paid holidays” is the noun phrase in an existential question, not a passive clause with “paid” as its main verb. “There” is also missing from nominal slots.
proposal.correction: Treat “are” as the existential predicate, “there” as its expletive, and “paid” as a modifier of “holidays”; include “there” in nominal slots.

findings.note: Existential are with paid modifying holidays. There has ADV POS in the actual parse, hence absent nominal slot; rebuild slots after correction.

baseline.semantic_caution: Ability, not riding completion.
Agreement with a proposition.
Counterfactual wish plus actual negative existential answer.
Evaluation and desire, not obtaining warm clothing.

proposal.explanation: “It” is capitalized mid-sentence after a comma; this is a capitalization typo.
proposal.correction: Change “It” to “it”.

findings.note: Mid-turn capitalization cleanup is not a structural mining error.

baseline.review_uncertainty: Great thanks: discourse evaluation vs adjective modifying thanks; avoid extracting an unsupported property.

baseline.semantic_caution: Elliptical affirmation depends on previous question.

baseline.review_uncertainty: good thing you can speak: possible content-clause versus relcl policy mismatch; do not force a change without schema decision.

proposal.explanation: “You can speak English” supplies the content of “a good thing”; it is not a relative clause modifying “thing.”
proposal.correction: Attach “speak” as a ccomp of “thing,” not a relcl.

findings.note: Content clause is not a relative clause; precise dependency convention must be retained when patching.

baseline.structural_issue: ham in ham sandwich is a common noun, not a proper name.

proposal.explanation: “Ham” is a common-noun modifier in “ham sandwich,” not a proper noun.
proposal.correction: Change token 3 to NOUN/NN.

findings.note: ham is NOUN/NN in the food compound.

baseline.semantic_caution: Price answer.
Confirmation of previous question.
Barber offering to brush hair off, not dismissing the interlocutor.
Commitment to take a message, not completion.

baseline.review_uncertainty: How much is a price question; inventory property must not be treated as affirmative fact. How POS minor.

baseline.semantic_caution: Epistemic disbelief, not inability.

proposal.explanation: In this copular question, “duties” is the subject and “What” is its complement; the two dependency labels are reversed.
proposal.correction: Label token 0 “What” as attr and token 5 “duties” as nsubj.

findings.note: Copular questions admit analysis alternatives. No demonstrated downstream semantic error; do not force label swap.

proposal.explanation: “For” introduces a prepositional phrase modifying “spell”; it is not a dative dependent.
proposal.correction: Change token 5 “for” from dative to prep, headed by “spell”; retain “me” as pobj.

findings.note: spaCy dative can label benefactive ADP for; conversion to prep is not required.

baseline.semantic_caution: Proposal, not going to cinema.
Acknowledgment, not visual perception.

baseline.source_issue: Repeated because-of-medals clause in source; not only is additive, not negation of love.

proposal.explanation: The phrase about medals is repeated before the final spirits reason, disrupting the not-only/but-also construction.
proposal.correction: Remove the duplicate phrase “but also because of many medals they've won,” (tokens 16–25).

findings.note: Duplicate medal reason is visible; preserve original until explicit source edit and rebase.

baseline.semantic_caution: Elliptical negative answer needs preceding proposition.
Hope for continued weather, not asserted future.

baseline.structural_issue: some is the requested object of get; advertised belongs to the embedded perception clause, not a get-resultative.

proposal.explanation: “Advertised” belongs to the relative-clause small clause selected by “saw,” not to “get.”
proposal.correction: Attach token 10 “advertised” to token 9 “saw” as its complement; retain “some” as the small-clause subject.

findings.note: Correctly identifies advertised scope, but retaining some as its subject is wrong. some is dobj of get; advertised belongs under saw.

baseline.semantic_caution: Performative thanking, not a request to thank.
Material description; passive form does not establish observed manufacturing.

baseline.structural_issue: on is a particle of try on; extra modifies small as degree, not a separate adjective property.

proposal.explanation: In “try it on,” on is the separated particle of try on, not a preposition; the particle construction is also missing.
proposal.correction: Set token 5 to prt and add a try on particle construction marked separated=true.

findings.note: try on particle correction is valid, but extra small degree morphology also needs review.

baseline.review_uncertainty: Why POS interrogative adverb versus SCONJ convention; minor.

baseline.structural_issue: tell coordinates with ask under may, not with have inside the embedded salary question.

proposal.explanation: Ask and tell are coordinated, but tell is attached to have and or to have, incorrectly placing the coordination inside the embedded question.
proposal.correction: Attach tell as a conjunct of ask (token 4) and attach or to ask.

findings.note: tell and or belong to ask rather than embedded have.

baseline.review_uncertainty: little degree adverb labelled amod; minor.

proposal.explanation: Little is an adverb modifying strange in “a little strange,” so amod does not match its POS or function.
proposal.correction: Change token 4’s dependency to advmod.

findings.note: little functions as degree adverb of strange; advmod is appropriate.

baseline.semantic_caution: Polite distancing request; needed is not proof the question was asked.
Agreement to a request, not performance.
Yeah follows a compound question; do not force which conjunct was affirmed.
Context-dependent question about chores.

proposal.explanation: What is the wh-complement of about, but it is attached with the generic dep relation.
proposal.correction: Attach What to about as its wh-complement rather than using dep.

findings.note: Generic dep in elliptical What about you is not sufficient evidence; the suggested wh-complement would compete with you.

baseline.structural_issue: lotus in lotus root is a common noun, not a proper name.

proposal.explanation: In the common-noun phrase lotus root, lowercase lotus is not a proper name.
proposal.correction: Tag lotus as NOUN/NN rather than PROPN/NNP.

findings.note: lotus is common NOUN/NN.

baseline.structural_issue: downwards and sideways are adverbs, not nouns. Coordinated minded has unresolved attribute target despite you shared subject.

proposal.explanation: Downwards and sideways describe the direction of looking; both are adverbs here, not nouns.
proposal.correction: Tag downwards and sideways as adverbs.

findings.note: downwards and sideways are adverbs. Do not turn the generalized cultural claim into approved factual semantics.

baseline.semantic_caution: Evaluation of a drink proposal; implicit subject remains unresolved.

baseline.review_uncertainty: for sure is an idiom, sure amod of ADP suspicious; one is nominal proform currently NUM, not literal quantity. Requires contract decision.

proposal.explanation: Sure is analyzed as an adjective modifying the preposition for, which does not fit the idiomatic phrase for sure.
proposal.correction: Analyze for sure as a phrase; do not make sure an amod of for.

findings.note: sure cannot be an ordinary adjectival modifier of ADP for; exact idiom representation needs a reviewed patch.

proposal.explanation: Big describes one, which refers back to the market; its property target is not null.
proposal.correction: Set big’s target to market (token 9), the referent of one.

findings.note: big syntactically modifies the proform one, not directly market. Null target is conservative; coreference is a separate layer.

baseline.review_uncertainty: late has controlled subject I but target null; conservative absence allowed, no asserted wrong property.

proposal.explanation: Late describes the understood subject of to be late, controlled by I; its property target is missing.
proposal.correction: Set late’s target to I (token 0).

findings.note: Controlled subject could enrich properties but conservative null target is allowed; not a wrong existing assertion.

baseline.review_uncertainty: due to is a compound preposition in spaCy-style parse; null adjective inventory alone is not an error.

baseline.structural_issue: Two independent roots around ellipsis: unfinished It is and restart Oh it is. Needs explicit boundary/repair treatment.

baseline.semantic_caution: Time answer; does not prove explanation credible.
Claim of ongoing friendly conversation is disputed by another speaker.

proposal.explanation: The first-person subject “I” does not agree with the annotated Person=3 feature on “was.”
proposal.correction: Set “was” to Person=1, or omit the person feature.

findings.note: Person=3 on was conflicts with explicit I. This was missed during the initial blind reading; added after inspection of API finding.

baseline.structural_issue: Two independently rooted utterances around ellipsis, let me write and I am ready; must not publish as one ordinary sentence.

proposal.explanation: In the permissive construction “let me write,” “me” is the object of “let,” and “write” is its open complement, not a ccomp.
proposal.correction: Attach “me” as dobj of “let” and “write” as xcomp of “let.”

findings.note: let me write uses the allowed nsubj/ccomp small-clause convention. The actual multi-root ellipsis boundary was missed.

baseline.structural_issue: Let me see and Sorry sir are independently rooted units; sir is also vocative.

proposal.explanation: In “let me see,” “me” is the object of “let,” and “see” is its open complement, not a ccomp.
proposal.correction: Attach “me” as dobj of “let” and “see” as xcomp of “let”.

findings.note: let me see uses the allowed nsubj/ccomp convention.

proposal.explanation: “Sir” directly addresses the listener, so it is a vocative rather than an npadvmod of “Sorry.”
proposal.correction: Mark “sir” as a vocative of “Sorry.”

findings.note: sir is vocative; independent-root sentence boundary remains missed.

baseline.semantic_caution: Name of market; passive called is not necessarily a completed naming event.

baseline.structural_issue: Second contracted s is has (active perfect become), not is/passive. it must be active subject.

proposal.explanation: Here “it’s become” means “it has become,” not passive “it is become”; the auxiliary and subject dependencies are therefore misanalyzed.
proposal.correction: Use lemma have and aux on token 10; attach token 9 as nsubj of “become.”

findings.note: Contracted has with active become and active subject.

baseline.semantic_caution: Reported evaluation, not independently verified ability.

baseline.structural_issue: has got expresses possession; contracted s and subject are incorrectly passive be/nsubjpass.

proposal.explanation: “She’s got” expresses possession with active “has got,” not a passive construction; the subject and auxiliary dependencies are misanalyzed.
proposal.correction: Attach token 2 as nsubj of “got”; use lemma have and aux for token 3.

findings.note: has got possession, not passive be.

baseline.semantic_caution: Plans reported, not executed.
Discourse request to pause, not evidence of waiting.

baseline.review_uncertainty: Discrepancy Fee capitalization does not establish a proper entity; get back to is conversational contact, not motion. Agreement is not payment.

baseline.semantic_caution: Offer received; admission remains conditional.

baseline.structural_issue: returns is a finite verb coordinated outside remember, not a noun/object coordinated with something.

proposal.explanation: “Returns” is a finite predicate coordinated with “seems,” not a noun coordinated with “something”; “and” should mark that predicate coordination.
proposal.correction: Tag “returns” as VERB/VBZ, attach it as a conjunct of “seems,” and attach “and” to “returns.”

findings.note: returns must be finite VERB/VBZ outside remember; spaCy cc should attach and to the preceding conjunct seems, not returns as proposed.

baseline.semantic_caution: Ongoing call with purpose, not completed query.
Desire to own a farm, not ownership.

baseline.review_uncertainty: Very carefully answers previous check question; should not be semantically attached to copular statement. when clause may admit alternative dependency labels.

proposal.explanation: The elliptical answer “Very carefully” is followed by an independent clause; the comma creates a likely boundary error in this dialogue context.
proposal.correction: Replace the comma after “carefully” with a period.

findings.note: Punctuation replacement is unnecessary. Preserve source and handle context-dependent elliptical answer, not a blanket comma-to-period edit.
